source_backup.create: sqlite3 source.backup(destination) against actual configured file
restore: Compare metadata database type with actual engine before restoration.
Copy existing configured file to .db.bak when present.
shutil.copy2 extracted SQLite database over configured path.
Only sqlite3.DatabaseError triggers copying saved .bak back before raising.
Actual restore task subsequently runs Django migrate; caught errors return backend SUCCESS with status=failed result.

deployment_static_facts: Default entrypoint provisions or waits for PostgreSQL and launches migrate/web via su-login.
Its explicit environment propagation whitelist omits DB_ENGINE.
Captured Compose examples use PostgreSQL defaults.
inferences_not_runtime_results: DB_ENGINE supplied to container may not reach actual login-shell application processes; effective default-entrypoint engine remains unmeasured.
Ungated PostgreSQL SQL in VOD0003 and Channels0038 likely blocks fresh SQLite migrations; exact first failure/applied prefix must be observed.

unguarded_postgres_operations: vod0003 DO blocks using pg_constraint and regclass

source_test_limit: Relevant backup unit tests mock SQLite dump/restore/engine branches; they do not establish physical SQLite application acceptance.
native_scope: Exact DB_ENGINE=sqlite is explicitly rejected before PG URL fallback.
Store is SQLx PgPool/PgRow with PG SQL/schema; sqlx enables postgres only.
Backup configuration requires PG URL and pg_dump/pg_restore/psql; creates PG members.
Normal restore uses PG database/server-generation and same Main PGpool fence; non-PG archive rejected.
SQLite requires coherent persistence/schema/history/file+WAL/connection/task+Beat and backup/restore lifecycles across real Main; adding archive member alone cannot meet it.
